claim: Memory Tax is an arXiv preprint (cs.CL) submitted 2026-10-25 by authors led from UIUC; not peer-reviewed.
Many dedicated agent memory systems underperform naive RAG over raw history, indicating negative net value (claimed, preprint).
quote: we find many dedicated memory systems underperform naive RAG in many cases, indicating a negative net value.

claim: Net value is split into memory benefit and memory tax, relative to direct retrieval.
quote: we dissect the net value of memory into the gains and losses over direct retrieval, termed memory benefit and memory tax .

claim: Study covers 11 memory systems, 3 benchmarks, 3 backbones; 90 of 99 memory results fall below naive RAG.
quote: 11 evaluated representative memory systems 90 / 99 memory results below Naive RAG 200 + experiment runs 20B+ tokens 10M+ LLM calls

claim: Memory systems usually cost far more than RAG without matching accuracy gains (authors' claim).
quote: Memory systems usually pay far more cost than RAG, but often without a matching gain in accuracy.

claim: Backbones were Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3.6-27B and GPT-5.6 Luna (low); answers judged by Qwen3.6-27B LLM-as-judge.
quote: We run every system on three backbones, Qwen3.5-4B , Qwen3.6-27B and GPT-5.6-luna(low) , sharing the same embedding model, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B . Answers are scored by an LLM-as-Judge backed by Qwen3.6-27B

claim: Two benchmarks were evaluated on stratified subsets (20% PersonaMem-v2, 10% MINT-Eval) due to cost.
quote: Due to cost constraints, we evaluate 20% of PersonaMem-v2 and 10% of MINT-Eval.

claim: Memory is not uniformly worse: it solves some queries RAG misses while losing others RAG solves.
quote: It does solve some queries RAG misses, where organization or restructuring may help, while losing others that RAG already solves.

claim: Information loss during memory construction directly causes memory tax.
quote: Information loss with varying severity during the memory process becomes a direct cause of memory tax.

claim: Memory processing reduces accessibility of evidence by fragmenting, diluting or rephrasing it.
quote: Memory process can reduce evidence accessibility by fragmenting, diluting, or rephrasing it, creating memory tax even evidence is not lost.

claim: Memory amplifies sensitivity to swapping the backbone model compared with RAG.
quote: Memory process can amplify backbone sensitivity since model-dependent operations can introduce additional variability to raw history.

claim: Simple baselines score high on many memory benchmarks: IDF-keyword >50% on some, RAG-Hybrid ~70%.
quote: the extremely simplified IDF-keyword based method can even achieve more than 50% in absolute score on some of them, while RAG-Hybrid reaches about 70%.

claim: In experiential memory, memory beats RAG on web tasks but falls behind on tool use.
quote: In web-based tasks, distilling long traces into workflows or strategies can outperform naive RAG, while for tool-use, several memory methods fall behind it

claim: Few prior memory papers reported a RAG baseline (only LightMem, PlugMem, Mem-T among those reviewed).
quote: we find that only three of them (excluding originally RAG system like HippoRAG2) report RAG results ( LightMem , PlugMem , and Mem-T )

claim: Authors argue naive RAG's strength is not due to a lucky configuration (ablations).
quote: suggesting that its performance is not driven by any particular component, careful tuning, or a lucky configuration .

claim: Proposed fix: keep a lightweight path back to source history (retrieve raw history alongside memory, rerank jointly).
quote: a more promising way to reduce memory tax is to make such deviations recoverable , preserving a lightweight path back to the source history when memory becomes insufficient.

claim: Authors frame memory as an implicit recommendation system predicting future relevance.
quote: memory can partly be seen as an implicit recommendation system that estimates future relevance of past information.

claim: Authors' stated limitations: non-exhaustive baselines, further tuning may help, static offline English benchmarks.
quote: our baseline selection is representative rather than exhaustive. We also follow official configurations wherever possible, though further system-specific tuning may yield better performance.

claim: PlugMem, an evaluated system, shares authors with the Memory Tax paper (Ke Yang, Xuan He, Jiawei Han, ChengXiang Zhai).
quote: Ke Yang, Zixi Chen, Xuan He, Jize Jiang, Michel Galley, Chenglong Wang, Jianfeng Gao, Jiawei Han, and ChengXiang Zhai. 2026a. Plugmem: A task-agnostic plugin memory module for llm agents.

claim: Per-baseline reproduction code is not yet released; eval results are on HF.
quote:
- [x] Release eval results in main experiments on HF
- [x] Release ablations, analysis results and other intermediates
- [ ] Release reproduction codes of each baseline

claim: Paper listed on Hugging Face Daily Papers on 2026-10-28 with 157 upvotes.
Independent preprint finds naive Raw-RAG ranks first in 6 of 7 benchmark-model settings vs agentic memory systems.
quote: Raw-RAG ranks first among the compared memory systems in six of seven benchmark-model settings, outperforming the strongest compared agentic memory system by 0.13-5.53 points.

claim: Independent preprint: raw chunked storage with zero LLM calls matches or beats lossy memory write strategies on LoCoMo.
quote: Raw chunked storage, which requires zero LLM calls, matches or outperforms expensive lossy alternatives

claim: Counterpoint: another evaluation finds no single memory substrate dominates; broad retrieval can harm sequential decision-making.
quote: no single substrate consistently dominates: broad retrieval benefits long-context factual QA, while excessive retrieval can harm sequential decision-making

claim: Vendor counterpoint (Vectorize/Hindsight): memory queries are not just document similarity problems, so RAG is often the wrong tool.
quote: RAG is often the wrong tool for memory because memory queries are not just document similarity problems.

claim: Press notes the study is a preprint and that the LLM judge is Qwen3.6-27B.
quote: The study is a preprint. It has not been peer reviewed, and the authors' own LLM judge is Qwen3.6-27B.
